ruling.recommended_action: Route this case to a human safety reviewer: log the rider's dangerous-driving allegation (speeding, hard braking, shoulder overtaking) and the driver's abusive written statement; retrieve the vehicle telemetry/GPS trace for independent corroboration; report per RydeHELP safety workflow and remind the rider of 995 / driver commercial insurance options if injured; consider a code-of-conduct review of the driver's abusive statement. Do not execute any fare adjustment automatically.
ruling.reasoning: Dispute type is safety, and the rider's complaint alleges dangerous driving throughout the trip (speeding, hard braking, overtaking on the shoulder) with the rider stating she felt scared and unsafe [F1][F2]. Under SAFE-2 the case must not be auto-adjudicated; the safety screen takes precedence over any fare/route analysis, so I rule escalate and provide a factual summary rather than a decision on the fare. Separately, the driver's written statement calls the rider "stupid" [F6] — hostile language aimed at the other party is abuse of a kind barred by Ryde's code of conduct (SAFE-1), so a safety concern is at least suspected on that basis too. Note the record is otherwise unremarkable: actual distance 10.5 km is 0.1 km shorter than the optimal 10.6 km and duration 15.9 min is short of the 16.5 min estimate [F1][F2], so there is no measurable route deviation to refund; the 2-message chat is fully timestamped [F3][F4][F5]; both profiles are clean with 0 disputes/0 upheld in 90 days [F7][F8], so no RD-6/NS-2 flag is triggered on this record. The dangerous-driving allegation is not resolvable from the fact table (no speed/telemetry facts, no traffic or incident facts), which is exactly why it goes to a human. Evidence status: sufficient for escalation purposes — the record settles that a safety allegation and an abusive driver statement exist; the underlying driving behaviour needs human investigation.
ruling.escalation_reason: Safety dispute: rider reports dangerous driving (speeding, harsh braking, shoulder overtaking) with fear for personal safety, and the driver's written statement contains an insult directed at the rider. Per SAFE-1/SAFE-2 no automatic ruling is issued; a human reviewer must assess the driving allegation and the conduct breach.

rejected_claims.reason: The driver's claim that 'I drove normally' cannot be credited against the rider's safety allegation: safety allegations are escalated for human review, and a written statement made after the trip is not evidence resolving a dangerous-driving claim.
No route-deviation claim arises: actual distance (10.5 km) is shorter than the optimal route (10.6 km) and duration was under estimate, so no off-route segment or RD-2 refund is supported.

safety_basis: Rider complaint alleges speeding, hard braking and overtaking on the shoulder throughout the trip, and that the rider felt scared and unsafe (dangerous-driving allegation, SAFE-2)
Driver's post-trip statement calls the rider 'stupid' — abusive language aimed at the other party, barred by Ryde's code of conduct (SAFE-1)
